author: Hugo de S. Victore
issue: Corpus Corporum's TEI transcription dropped the Hebrew type Migne set inline (Hebrew followed by a Latin transliteration), leaving a stray space or doubled comma. Recovered from the plates and re-inserted into both Latin and English twins. See hebrew-recovery.md for the method.

source.note: IIIF image API works though info.json/viewer 403. Native scan ~1860px/page. Front-matter Roman cols end ~f70; Arabic col C ≈ f70 + (C-9)/2.

patches.note: Consonantal, unpointed as Migne set it. Reading matches Migne's own transliteration (Biflagoth ruben ... helchiche lem) and the Masoretic text of Judg 5:15b. The Gallica scan is low-res and the type imperfect, leaving ל/ר (first word) and ה/ח (last word) indistinct at pixel level; read per MT + transliteration. A sharper copy (Google Books JoXYAAAAMAAJ) could confirm the two glyphs if ever needed.
Pointed, legible; matches MT (šôq) ʿal-yārēk — Migne prints only the 'upon the thigh' portion. Was the doubled-comma lacuna.
Migne's doublet on the root ḥ-m-r (ass / heap), glossed 'cumulum de cumulis'. MT of the verse reads ḥămôr ḥămōrātayim; Hugh/Migne give the shortened doublet as printed.

notLacuna.finding: NO Hebrew type on the plate — 'In Hebraeo habetur: Romae Zachae ...' runs straight into the transliteration. The translation agent inferred a dropped lacuna here, but the scan shows the transliteration is complete. No patch; crux note corrected. Lesson: the scan is the arbiter — not every 'In Hebraeo' spot carries Hebrew type.
